The Washing of the Feet

Scriptural scenes

The Washing of the Feet

Christ Washing the Disciples’ Feet · Nipter

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

John 13:1–17

King James Version · Scripture previews

This sixteenth-century Stavronikita fresco by Theophanes the Cretan depicts Christ washing the disciples’ feet. The image remains a complete historic reproduction.

[1] Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field title; Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.ImageDescription; Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.DateTimeOriginal; Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Artist; Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.Credit; Exact file record File:Washing of the feet - Stavronikita monastery, Mt Athos - Theophanes of Crete, 16th c..jpg,field imageinfo.extmetadata.LicenseShortName

What is depicted

Christ bends before a seated disciple with a basin below; the other disciples gather around. The monastery and painter are identified in the exact file record. These visible actions are distinguished from the liturgical foot-washing rite.

History and tradition

He riseth from supper, and laid aside his garments; and took a towel, and girded himself.

After that he poureth water into a bason, and began to wash the disciples’ feet, and to wipe them with the towel wherewith he was girded.

[2] John 13:4–5

Published explanation

So after he had washed their feet, and had taken his garments, and was set down again, he said unto them, Know ye what I have done to you?

Ye call me Master and Lord: and ye say well; for so I am.

If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another’s feet.

For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you.

Verily, verily, I say unto you, The servant is not greater than his lord; neither he that is sent greater than he that sent him.

If ye know these things, happy are ye if ye do them.

Christ’s words in John’s Gospel; no additional service rubric or invented visitor action is added.

[2] John 13:12–17
